title: eval-harness: add per-prompt CI metrics hook and quality gating
author: Maya Patel
description:
Motivation: we need finer-grained regression detection for prompt-set evaluations. Existing CI gates run aggregate evals which can hide regressions that affect a small subset of prompts. This PR adds a per-prompt metrics CI hook, an opt-in quality gating layer, and instrumentation to surface per-prompt regressions as GitHub annotations and dashboard metrics.

What this changes: adds a new GitHub Actions workflow that runs the eval-harness per-prompt job, a lightweight hook which computes per-prompt metrics and compares them against historical baselines, integration code to publish results to our metrics pipeline, and docs/runbook for teams to opt in. The per-prompt gate is opt-in via a repo-level config flag and supports configurable thresholds and a whitelist of prompt-sets to ignore.

Checklist:
- [x] Add per-prompt CI workflow and job
- [x] Implement per_prompt_hook.py that computes metrics and emits annotations
- [x] Expose per-prompt metrics from runner and wire into existing metrics exporter
- [x] Add unit tests and an end-to-end smoke test for the workflow (runs as a fast subset)
- [x] Update docs and runbook
- [x] Add telemetry so SRE/observability can track false positives

Why opt-in: teams owning large prompt catalogs may have noisy prompts; opt-in prevents platform-wide false positives while giving teams control. We also added conservative default thresholds and a manual override to allow merging with a documented risk justification.

Compatibility: no breaking API changes to existing eval-harness public APIs. The new hook is backwards-compatible and disabled unless configured.

Notes on reliability: the workflow uploads an artifact payload and the hook runs a lightweight summarizer to keep CI runtimes under the existing SLO (workflow adds ~6m on average when running full check; default runs a fast sample).

summary: Adds per-prompt metrics CI hook, opt-in quality gating, new workflow, exporter updates, tests and docs. Gate is conservative and opt-in; provides GitHub annotations and metrics integration.
notes_for_release: Teams can opt-in to per-prompt gating by adding eval_harness: { per_prompt_gate: enabled } to their repo config. Defaults are conservative to minimize noise.
merge_notes: Merged via squash after approvals and CI green. Kept individual commits for history but used squash commit to main.
